text:
alex: Hey team — running into a weird one on the sampleapp onboarding flow after upgrading the Node embed SDK to v1.12. The rerank step throws a
alex: "vector length mismatch: expected 768 got 770" error in staging. Not sure if batching helper or response formatting changed.
alex: Minimal repro snippet from the client request:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "model": "open-embed-768",
  "input": ["doc1", "doc2"],
  "batch_size": 2
}
```
alex: Response we got (truncated):
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.012,0.34,...,0.99]},{"embedding":[0.011,0.33,...,0.98]}],"model":"open-embed-768"}
```
alex: But when the reranker receives the vectors, its shape inspector logs 770 length for second vector. 🤔

maria: Did you check if the Node SDK is appending metadata fields into the embedding array accidentally? We had a bug where auth retry inserted an extra trailing 0 for a NULL field.
maria: Also, which exact SDK call? sampleapp uses embed.batch() vs embed.create() differences.

alex: sampleapp uses embed.batch() from the new helper. I grepped and didn't find any manual concat. Strange thing: Python sample doesn't show the issue.

jordan: Could be header-related. We had a parity issue where Node was sending Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 and the proxy did a different parsing path that flattened arrays oddly.
jordan: Can you paste the raw response bytes (curl --raw) so we can verify no stray chars? Also include the X-Request-Id from the logs.

alex: Raw bytes attached (pasted): shows correct JSON. X-Request-Id: rq_01H8X9

sam-k: I remember a flaky case where the batching helper would coerce typed arrays to regular arrays, and a small rounding step added an extra element when converting Float32Array -> Array in Node v18. That could explain +2 mismatch.
sam-k: On top of that, if auth refresh triggers a replay, duplicate merges can lead to odd lengths. Any retries in the logs?

alex: There's one 401 then a retry in the client logs right before the bad batch: auth-refresh happened, token refreshed, embed call retried by the helper.

maria: Ok that's promising. Two hypotheses:
- retry + merge bug in client-side batch helper appends a sentinel 0 when merging partial batches
- alternate parsing path due to charset header in proxy

maria: Quick check: can you run the Node sampleapp with env DEBUG=embed:batch and attach the trace? Also try forcing Content-Type to exactly application/json (no charset) as an experiment.

alex: Will run that now and report back. If it's helper-related I can patch to dedupe/reassign length before calling reranker.

deploybot: deploybot: Staging rollout 2025-03-22T16:18:00Z complete for sampleapp (sha: a1b2c3)

jordan: If this repros locally, let's add an assert in the SDK: throw if embedding array length != model.dim and include request id. That will make debugging easier for customers.

sam-k: Agree. Also add a small unit that converts Float32Array -> Array by mapping and not using typed buffer.slice or toJSON which had edge cases.

alex: Update: local run with DEBUG logs shows the retry merge inserted an empty numeric slot (0) between vectors. For now I trimmed arrays before rerank and the pipeline succeeds. I'll open a PR to fix helper merge and add an SDK regression test using auth-fail then replay.

maria: Awesome. Can you link the PR here and include the failing log snippet so we can cut a patch release? 🙏

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/438
alex: Pasted failing snippet in the PR description. I'll also add a sampleapp test that toggles BATCH_MERGE_STRICT=true to exercise.

jordan: Nice work. After the patch, let's run the end-to-end against the rerank harness to validate no silent dim drift.

sam-k: Also add a small note in the devex doc about "auth-retry + batch-merge" gotcha so solutions engineers can triage faster.

alex: Will do. Thanks folks :thumbsup:
